method.visualInspection: 1 fps contact sheets and targeted composition inspection; event boundaries approximate to ±0.5 s, not hand-verified on every decoded frame.
method.speech: Gemini word-timed transcription retained privately with source media; proper-name transcription may be wrong. No copied narration in the new scripts.
method.frameIndex: Every decoded frame indexed with timestamp and normalized low-resolution inter-frame change. This detects candidate edit boundaries; it is not semantic visual inspection.
method.adaptation: Reference mechanics adapted to neutral sculpture, white cards, gray instruments and Mogging typography; no claim of exact 1:1 fidelity.

references.title: Philtrum: a measured relationship

events.observation: Immediate same-face length comparison; slider, value and grade change together.
Push toward the nose and upper lip. Endpoints establish the local vertical interval.
Hold the close crop; move the mouth/upper-lip region while the short bracket follows.
Change the demonstrated model and its reference range; preserve the graphic grammar.
Pull back, acquire corners, then the brief product close.

notes: Question → locate → sex-specific range → consequence → invitation.
The continuous face and persistent readout connect the explanation.
Do not adopt the reference’s ideal ranges, age inference or grade as verified evidence.

references.title: Jaw angle: construct, reveal, fold

events.observation: Profile establishes two jaw-corner states before explaining the construction.
Push toward the ear; draw the descending ramus guide first.
Draw the lower mandibular guide toward the chin. Stagger the angular arc after both legs.
Registered mandible/teeth cutaway fades onto the same face. Small angle readout sits at the vertex.
Hinge the rear guide about the jaw corner until it lies along the lower guide; a ratio annotation follows.
Open and close the jaw corner while slider, angle and descriptive state respond.
Pull back, restore the baseline, acquire corners and close.

notes: Question → two-leg definition → bone context → ratio demonstration → contrasting extremes → invitation.
The folding guide is an explanatory action, not decoration.
Golden-ratio, ideal-angle and attractiveness claims are unverified; our model uses relative settings.

references.title: Perspective: keep the face framed

events.observation: Same frontal face changes apparent proportions; a distance ruler remains persistent.
Bracket the nasal region; faint dimension grids and reference lines support the explanation.
Matched feature insets distinguish nose, face width and ear visibility.
An elliptical mirror/sweep graphic punctuates the comparison.
Camera-distance example, constrained eye line and compensated framing make the variable legible.
Return to the complete face with scanning brackets and the close.

notes: Demonstration statement → physical explanation → visible consequences → familiar comparison → practical setup → invitation.
Use an actual perspective camera and compensate field of view; never fake perspective by stretching pixels.
Reference “better” judgments and exact recommended distances are not a calibrated personal assessment.

references.title: Brows: comparison before explanation

events.observation: Two small registered image cards make the eyebrow/no-eyebrow contrast visible. Cards expand and merge.
Return to a large face. Local brow appearance changes while the rest of the face stays put.
Localized contrast demonstration with persistent control panel and compact research attribution.
Pull back to the face, corners and short invitation.

notes: Research-led opening → recognizable difference → feature-specific claim → a second variable → invitation.
Distinct cuts compress the argument while retaining the same subject and camera.
Density, shape and contrast are different variables. Our current fiber material control demonstrates contrast only.

references.title: Cheeks: build a coordinate system

events.observation: One frontal face demonstrates a higher/lower cheek position; the setting is visible before its definition.
Draw the pupil datum, then a second horizontal line at the upper lip.
Locate the widest cheek region; add width/vertical relations and faint underlying bone patches.
Move that landmark vertically with the shape; the face, shadow and slider remain connected.
Restore and pull back into the closing scan frame.

notes: Binary question → locating procedure → relative position → visual contrast → invitation.
The guides are introduced in spoken order rather than appearing all at once.
A sculpture’s cheek anchor can be surface-bound; a real portrait still needs its own registered anatomy.

references.title: Midface: plane and signed relationship

events.observation: Front/angled face with an upper-jaw cutaway; orient to a profile for the test.
Locate the brow/glabella datum and drop a vertical reference plane.
Add a short horizontal relationship from the nasal base to that plane.
Morph the midface support; maintain the reference plane and small signed offset readout.
Reinforce the related nose/lip/cheek changes in a close profile crop.
Pull out, acquire and close.

notes: Provocative question → orient → locate → compare to a datum → visible relationships → invitation.
The reference plane persists while the feature moves, creating a stable explanation.
We do not reproduce the reference’s diagnosis from a photo; this is an illustrative dimensional model.

references.title: Recessed jaw: three-point profile construction

events.observation: Preview two jaw states on the same face, then reset.
Turn to profile and place the brow, under-nose, and chin points separately.
Pull back to preserve all three marks. Draw both legs and reveal the angle.
Hold the profile while the chin position and guide move together.
Restore the face and move the guide into a scan outro.

notes: Full clip sampled at 3 fps. Selected motion examined at its native 30 fps and compared with the creator-provided caption timings.
Use the choreography. Any facial thresholds or aesthetic, health or treatment claims from the reference require independent validation.

references.title: Brow height relative to the eye opening

events.observation: Preview low and high positions in a matched crop.
Draw the pupil datum before building the first gap.
Add the eye opening as a separate reference length.
Morph brow height while both guides remain registered.

notes: Full clip sampled at 3 fps. Selected motion examined at its native 30 fps and compared with the creator-provided caption timings.
Use the choreography. Any facial thresholds or aesthetic, health or treatment claims from the reference require independent validation.

references.title: Bone and surface: scan and separate

events.observation: A horizontal light bar travels down. It reveals bone behind the moving edge.
The surface retracts to a card and a second card turns out from behind it.
Return to the same face with thin contour bands across the cheeks.
Change the demonstrated support and retain the framing so the shadow change is legible.

notes: Full clip sampled at 3 fps. Selected motion examined at its native 30 fps and compared with the creator-provided caption timings.
